canonical.title: Topological Sort of a DAG
canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/3. Topo Sort Problems/01. Topological Sorting.cpp

narrative.title: The Assembly-Line Sequencing Sheet
narrative.scenario: A factory's installation manual lists one-way dependency tickets between workstations: certain stations must finish before others may start. The planner needs one legal run order — any order where every ticket's predecessor comes first. With no loops guaranteed, a finish-time walk down the ticket map, read backwards, produces a valid sequence.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer nodes and an edge list graph where each entry [u, v] is a one-way dependency u -> v. The graph is a DAG.
narrative.outputFormat: Return a topological order — a permutation of 0..nodes-1 in which every edge u -> v has u appearing before v.
constraints: The graph is directed and acyclic

testCases.explanation: 0 must precede 1 and 2, and both must precede 3 — this order satisfies every ticket.
Station 2 has no predecessors and lands first; 0 and 1 are free afterwards.

hintLevels: Level 1: A node can be released once everything it depends on has been released.
Level 2: DFS appends nodes on the way OUT of the recursion; reversing that finish-time list yields the order.
Level 3: Sweep all nodes as DFS roots — disconnected DAG parts each contribute their own finish chain.
